title: China-to-Kenya Wireless / IoT Device Compliance Gap Matrix (CA / KEBS)
provenance: AI-compiled, multi-model cross-checked, not human-verified. Informational only; confirm with the official regulator and a qualified professional. Not legal/certification/customs/market-access advice.

rows.requirement: CA Type Approval — Radio and Telecommunications Terminal Equipment
rows.target_requirement: All radio transmitters and telecommunications terminal equipment must obtain a CA type approval certificate from the Communications Authority of Kenya before importation or sale in Kenya, under the Kenya Information and Communications Act Cap 411A and associated type approval regulations. The CA mark must appear on the product and its packaging. CE marking, FCC authorisation, and CCC certification are not recognised as equivalents by the CA.
target_standards: Kenya Information and Communications Act Cap 411A
Communications Authority of Kenya Type Approval Regulations
rows.china_equivalent: China MIIT SRRC radio type approval for radio frequency equipment; MIIT network access licence (NAL) for telecommunications terminal equipment; CCC certification for RF equipment within CCC scope. GB standards (e.g. GB 15844, GB 8702) apply domestically. SRRC, NAL, and CCC approvals are China-domestic only and carry no legal standing with the Communications Authority of Kenya.
china_standards: MIIT Network Access Licence (NAL) — Telecommunications Terminal Equipment (China)
China Compulsory Certification (CCC) — RF equipment in scope (China)
rows.gap: Mandatory separate CA type approval certificate required from the Communications Authority of Kenya. CE, FCC, and CCC approvals are not accepted. SRRC and NAL have no legal standing in Kenya. The CA mark must be displayed on product label and packaging.
rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] CA type approval is mandatory for all radio and telecommunications terminal equipment imported or sold in Kenya. Chinese SRRC, NAL, and CCC approvals are not recognised by the CA. A separate CA type approval process must be completed and the CA mark displayed on the product and packaging.

rows.requirement: Cybersecurity — CA IoT Advisory Guidelines (Kenya National Cybersecurity Strategy)
rows.target_requirement: Kenya does not currently have a mandatory IoT device cybersecurity certification scheme. The Communications Authority of Kenya (CA) has issued advisory guidelines for IoT security recommending baseline security practices such as unique device credentials, secure software update mechanisms, and encryption of sensitive data. The Kenya National Cybersecurity Strategy provides the broader policy framework. Compliance with CA IoT advisory guidelines is recommended but not legally mandated at this time. The regulatory landscape may evolve; exporters should monitor CA publications for mandatory requirements.
target_standards: Communications Authority of Kenya — IoT Security Advisory Guidelines
Kenya Information and Communications Act Cap 411A (general regulatory authority)
rows.china_equivalent: China has issued IoT security standards including GB/T 37093 (IoT security requirements) and GB/T 36951 (IoT information security evaluation), along with MIIT guidance on IoT security. These are advisory or recommended standards in China and are not recognised by the Communications Authority of Kenya. CCC does not cover IoT cybersecurity.
china_standards: GB/T 37093 — IoT Security Requirements (China, recommended standard)
GB/T 36951 — IoT Information Security Evaluation (China, recommended standard)
rows.gap: No mandatory IoT cybersecurity certification exists in Kenya at this time. CA advisory guidelines recommend baseline security practices for IoT devices. Chinese GB/T 37093 and related standards are not recognised by the CA. Exporters should document their device security baseline and monitor CA and Kenya National Cybersecurity Authority publications for any emerging mandatory requirements.
rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] There is no mandatory IoT cybersecurity certification in Kenya at this time. CA advisory guidelines recommend baseline IoT security practices. Chinese GB/T 37093 and related standards are not recognised by the CA. Exporters should implement reasonable security baselines and monitor CA publications for future mandatory requirements.

rows.requirement: Electrical Safety — 240V/50Hz Type-G Plug (KS IEC 62368-1 / PVOC)
rows.target_requirement: Kenya operates on 240V/50Hz with type-G plugs (British 3-pin square, BS 1363 equivalent). Wireless and IoT devices with power adapters or direct mains connections must comply with the Kenya Standard KS IEC 62368-1 for audio/video, information and communications technology equipment safety. Electrical safety compliance is also verified through the PVOC (Pre-Export Verification of Conformity) process conducted at the Chinese factory before shipment. Products must be adapted for the 240V/50Hz type-G environment; 220V or type-A/C plug configurations used in China are not suitable without modification.
target_standards: KS IEC 62368-1 — Audio/Video, Information and Communications Technology Equipment Safety (Kenya Standard)
Kenya PVOC (Pre-Export Verification of Conformity) Programme
BS 1363 — Type-G Plug and Socket (applicable reference for plug compatibility)
rows.china_equivalent: China uses 220V/50Hz with type-A and type-I plugs. Electrical safety is covered by GB 4943.1 (information technology equipment safety, adopting IEC 62368-1) under the CCC mandatory certification scheme. CCC test reports from CNCA-accredited laboratories are China-domestic only and are not recognised by KEBS or accepted as a substitute for PVOC verification.
china_standards: GB 4943.1 — Information Technology Equipment Safety (China, adopting IEC 62368-1)
China Compulsory Certification (CCC) — Electrical and Electronic Equipment
rows.gap: Kenya's 240V/50Hz type-G environment requires hardware adaptation (plug type and voltage range) and separate KS IEC 62368-1 safety compliance. CCC certification is not recognised. PVOC verification at the Chinese factory by an accredited inspection body (Bureau Veritas, SGS, or Intertek) is required before shipment for regulated product categories.
rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Electrical safety compliance under KS IEC 62368-1 and PVOC pre-export verification are required for mains-powered wireless and IoT devices exported from China to Kenya. Products must be adapted for Kenya's 240V/50Hz type-G plug environment. Chinese CCC certification is not accepted as an equivalent.

source.publisher: Kenya Bureau of Standards (KEBS) — PVOC Programme

rows.requirement: KEBS EMC — Radiated and Conducted Emissions (KS IEC 55032)
rows.target_requirement: Multimedia and wireless equipment must comply with Kenya Standard KS IEC 55032 (adopting IEC 55032) for electromagnetic emissions limits. Compliance is assessed by a KEBS-recognised laboratory. The KEBS Diamond Mark indicates product quality conformity with KS standards and may be required for regulated electronics on the Kenya market.
target_standards: KS IEC 55032 — Multimedia Equipment: Electromagnetic Emissions (Kenya Standard)
rows.china_equivalent: China GB/T 9254 (adopting CISPR 32) covers EMC emissions for multimedia equipment. GB/T 9254 test reports are generated by China CNAS-accredited laboratories and support domestic CCC or self-declaration. These reports are not directly accepted by KEBS but may serve as a technical baseline for KS IEC 55032 testing.
china_standards: GB/T 9254 — Information Technology Equipment: Radio Disturbance Characteristics (China, adopting CISPR 32)
rows.gap: Kenya requires compliance with KS IEC 55032 assessed by a KEBS-recognised laboratory. Chinese GB/T 9254 test reports are not directly accepted by KEBS. Separate KS IEC 55032 testing and KEBS Diamond Mark certification may be required for regulated product categories.
rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] KS IEC 55032 EMC emissions compliance, assessed by a KEBS-recognised laboratory, is required for multimedia and wireless equipment in Kenya. Chinese GB/T 9254 reports are not directly accepted. KEBS Diamond Mark certification applies to regulated product categories.

rows.target_requirement: Multimedia equipment must also meet immunity requirements under Kenya Standard KS IEC 55035 (adopting IEC 55035). This standard applies to immunity against electromagnetic disturbances for multimedia equipment including wireless and IoT devices. Testing must be conducted at a KEBS-recognised laboratory.
target_standards: KS IEC 55035 — Multimedia Equipment: Electromagnetic Immunity (Kenya Standard)
rows.china_equivalent: China GB/T 17618 (adopting CISPR 35) addresses EMC immunity for multimedia equipment. Domestic test reports from CNAS-accredited laboratories support CCC or self-declaration processes. These are not directly recognised by KEBS for Kenya market access.
china_standards: GB/T 17618 — Information Technology Equipment: Immunity Characteristics (China, adopting CISPR 35)
rows.gap: Separate KS IEC 55035 immunity testing at a KEBS-recognised laboratory is required. Chinese GB/T 17618 test reports are not directly accepted for KEBS certification. Both emissions (KS IEC 55032) and immunity (KS IEC 55035) must be addressed for full EMC compliance in Kenya.
rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] KS IEC 55035 immunity testing is required alongside KS IEC 55032 emissions testing for full EMC compliance of multimedia and wireless equipment in Kenya. Chinese GB/T 17618 reports are not directly recognised by KEBS.

rows.requirement: Local Importer / Authorised Dealer and PVOC Certificate
rows.target_requirement: A locally registered Kenya importer or authorised dealer is required for CA type approval registration and market entry. Importers must be registered with the Communications Authority of Kenya. In addition, the PVOC (Pre-Export Verification of Conformity) programme administered by KEBS requires that regulated electronics exports to Kenya obtain a PVOC certificate of conformity issued by a KEBS-accredited inspection body (Bureau Veritas, SGS, or Intertek) at the factory in China before shipment. The PVOC certificate must accompany the goods on arrival at the port of entry.
target_standards: Kenya Information and Communications Act Cap 411A — importer registration requirement
KEBS PVOC Programme — Pre-Export Verification of Conformity for regulated imports
Kenya Bureau of Standards Legal Notice No. 103 (PVOC designated products)
rows.china_equivalent: China has no domestic equivalent to the Kenya PVOC requirement. For China-domestic sales, the manufacturer or a domestic distributor handles CCC registration without a pre-export verification obligation. Chinese exporters must engage a KEBS-accredited inspection body (Bureau Veritas, SGS, or Intertek) at the factory or in China to obtain the PVOC certificate before shipment to Kenya.
china_standards: No China-domestic equivalent to PVOC; CCC registration (China) covers domestic market entry only
rows.gap: No China-domestic process maps to the Kenya PVOC requirement. Chinese exporters must engage a KEBS-accredited inspection body in China (Bureau Veritas, SGS, or Intertek) to obtain a PVOC certificate before shipment. A locally registered Kenya importer or authorised dealer must also be appointed for CA registration purposes. Both requirements must be satisfied before goods arrive at the Kenyan port of entry.
rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] A Kenya-registered local importer or authorised dealer is mandatory for CA registration. A PVOC certificate from a KEBS-accredited body (Bureau Veritas, SGS, or Intertek) obtained at the Chinese factory before shipment is required for regulated electronics exports to Kenya. There is no China-domestic equivalent to PVOC.
